n: Merchants weighed goods on balance scales. Rigging the scale or using a false weight cheats people, and God detests it; honest weights delight him. Business ethics are spiritual matters.

f.g: Stones of standard weight used to measure silver or goods.

n: Pride leads to disgrace, but humility brings wisdom.

f.w: When pride cometh, then cometh shame

n: Integrity guides honest people like a compass, but crookedness destroys the treacherous.

f.g: Hebrew tummah—wholeness, being complete and undivided.

n: Riches can’t save anyone on the day of judgment; only righteousness can.
The righteousness of the blameless makes their road straight; the wicked trip over their own wickedness.

f.g: Makes his path straight and smooth.

n: Righteousness rescues the upright, but the treacherous are trapped by their own evil desires.

f.g: naughtiness = wickedness, evil craving (stronger than modern usage).

n: When a wicked person dies, all their hopes die with them. Their plans were built only for this life.
The righteous are rescued from trouble, and the wicked fall into it in their place—as happened when Haman was hanged on his own gallows.

f.w: the wicked cometh in his stead

n: A godless person destroys neighbors with words, but knowledge rescues the righteous.

f.g: Hebrew ḥanef—godless, profane person.

n: A whole city celebrates when good people prosper and when the wicked fall. Public life is shaped by private character.
The blessings of upright citizens lift a city up, but the words of the wicked tear it down.
Belittling your neighbor shows a lack of sense; a wise person knows when to stay quiet.

f.g: Keeps silent.

n: A gossip betrays confidences, but a trustworthy person keeps a secret.

f.g: talebearer = gossip, one who spreads rumors.

n: Without guidance a nation falls, but many advisers bring safety. Good decisions come from seeking counsel.

f.w: in the multitude of counsellors there is safety

n: Guaranteeing a stranger’s debt will hurt you; refusing such deals keeps you safe.

f.g: smart = suffer painfully.
suretiship = the practice of guaranteeing another’s debt.

n: A gracious woman gains honor, just as ruthless men gain wealth. The contrast suggests honor won by grace is better than riches seized by force.

f.g: Possibly “ruthless” or “violent men.”

n: Kindness benefits the kind person; cruelty hurts the one who is cruel.

f.w: The merciful man doeth good to his own soul

n: Wicked gains are deceptive and won’t last, but sowing righteousness brings a sure reward.
True righteousness leads to life; chasing evil leads to death.
The Lord detests the crooked in heart but delights in those whose ways are blameless.
Even if the wicked join forces, they won’t escape punishment; the righteous and their descendants will be rescued.

f.g: Possibly “be assured” (a pledge with the hand), or “even if they band together.”

n: A vivid, humorous image: a beautiful woman with no sense is like a gold ring in a pig’s nose—beauty wasted on what can’t honor it.

f.w: a jewel of gold in a swine's snout
f.g: Nose rings were common jewelry; pigs were unclean and rooted in the mud.
discretion = good sense, judgment.

n: The righteous desire only good; the hopes of the wicked end in wrath.

f.w: The desire of the righteous is only good

n: A paradox of generosity: some give freely and grow richer; others hoard and grow poorer.

f.g: meet = fitting, right.

n: A generous person will prosper; whoever refreshes others will be refreshed.

f.w: The liberal soul shall be made fat
f.g: liberal = generous; made fat = enriched, prospered.

f.w: he that watereth shall be watered also himself

n: People curse someone who hoards grain to raise prices in a shortage, but they bless the one who sells it fairly.

f.g: corn = grain (wheat or barley), not maize.

n: Whoever seeks good finds goodwill; whoever looks for trouble will find it.

f.g: procureth = obtains, gains.

n: Those who trust in riches will fall, but the righteous will flourish like green leaves.

f.w: He that trusteth in his riches shall fall

f.g: Or “like a green leaf.”

n: Whoever brings trouble on their own family inherits only wind—nothing. The fool ends up serving the wise.

f.g: Gain nothing of substance.

n: The life of the righteous is like a tree of life, and the one who wins people’s hearts is wise. Latter-day Saints often apply the second line to sharing the gospel.

f.w: he that winneth souls is wise

n: If even the righteous face consequences in this life, how much more will the wicked. Peter quotes this verse (from the Greek version).

f.g: recompensed = repaid, given what is due.

f.w: much more the wicked and the sinner
